tools.description: Look up notes by name the user typed: every word of `name` must match a word of a note title or alias (case and Vietnamese diacritics ignored); an exact vault path also works. Returns id, title, type, aliases. Use it first whenever the user names something. Several hits that are different things (two people with similar names): ask the user which one, do not pick. Hits that are the same thing (duplicate notes): say so.

limit.description: Items shown before the result is summarised (default 20). Long results return count, by_type, the first items and a handle for `more`.

tools.name: find

tools.description: Read one note: type, frontmatter properties, aliases, validity window, provenance fields (status, proposed_by, extracted_by, asserted_at), edge counts by relation and layer, block ids, and the start of the body. For a claim note also the edge it asserts.

body_chars.description: Characters of body text to include (default 800, 0 = none).

node.description: Note id = vault path exactly as returned by find/other tools, e.g. "Khách hàng/Công ty ABC.md".

tools.name: note

tools.description: Typed edges around one note, one step. Each item: rel (name in walking direction; incoming edges use the inverse name, e.g. has_project for an incoming client edge), node, type, dir, status and layer (accepted | proposed), claim (the claim note behind a causal/fact edge), valid_from/valid_to, source (note#^block), proposed_by, extracted_by, confidence. Good for "what is X connected to", "who works at X now" (rels + as_of), "what increases X" (dir in).

accepted_only.description: true = drop machine-suggested (proposed) edges; keep only what the user wrote or approved.

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Only edges whose validity window (valid_from..valid_to) contains this day: who works where, which contract/claim held then. Use today for "now/currently/đang". Omit = ignore time.

dir.description: out = edges written on this note (forward), in = edges pointing at it, both (default).

limit.description: Items shown before the result is summarised (default 20). Long results return count, by_type, the first items and a handle for `more`.

node.description: Note id = vault path exactly as returned by find/other tools, e.g. "Khách hàng/Công ty ABC.md".

rels.description: Only these relation names (forward names from the server instructions; inverse names are produced automatically when walking backwards). Omit = all relations.

statuses.description: Edge layers counted. Default: accepted + superseded + proposed (machine suggestions, marked layer "proposed"). ["proposed"] = only unreviewed suggestions.

tools.name: neighbors

tools.description: Every note reachable from `node` by repeatedly following edges, start excluded, with the smallest depth when max_depth is set. dir "out" = downstream (everything X leads to / affects / causes), "in" = upstream (everything that leads to / influences X). One call answers broad multi-hop questions ("all factors that eventually drive revenue"); do not walk neighbors step by step for that. Long results are summarised by type; report the count and grouping rather than copying every id.

tools.description: Top-k simple directed paths from one note to another (shortest first), at most max_len edges. Each path: nodes, rels, statuses per step, sign (+/-, net effect from relation polarity: increases +, decreases/prevents -), layer (accepted only if every step is accepted). Use for "how does X affect Y", "why", "is X connected to Y".

tools.description: Feedback loops (simple directed cycles) through one note, at most max_len edges; both are required (whole-vault cycle search is too expensive). Each loop: nodes (starting at `node`), rels, negatives (number of negative links), kind (reinforcing if even, balancing if odd), layer. Use rels = causal relations (increases, decreases, prevents, conditions) for vicious/virtuous circles.

tools.description: Where a claim (or any note) comes from: cited sources with the #^block they point to, notes that support or dispute it, record (status, proposed_by, extracted_by, asserted_at, validity window), the edge it asserts, and the chain of notes that superseded it.

claim.description: Note id = vault path exactly as returned by find/other tools, e.g. "Khách hàng/Công ty ABC.md".

tools.name: provenance

tools.description: Notes whose frontmatter matches every given key = value (string compare). Named filters: `type` (note type), `status` (review state: proposed = waiting for the user to review, accepted, superseded, rejected) and `proposed_by` (WHO proposed it: llm, model, rule, human). These are different: "created / proposed by the AI/LLM" = proposed_by "llm" (any status, any type); "waiting for review" = status "proposed" (by anyone). Other keys go in `where`. Use for listing notes of a type, e.g. type "tool" for the tools / software the user works with.

limit.description: Items shown before the result is summarised (default 20). Long results return count, by_type, the first items and a handle for `more`.

where.description: Other frontmatter key: value pairs, e.g. {"confidence": "established"}.

tools.name: select

tools.description: Notes of one type whose own validity window (valid_from..valid_to) contains a day: contracts, decisions, price lists, claims in force on that date.

limit.description: Items shown before the result is summarised (default 20). Long results return count, by_type, the first items and a handle for `more`.

type.description: Note type, e.g. contract, decision, claim.

tools.name: valid

tools.description: Notes related to search hits, ranked by personalised PageRank over the typed graph (both directions). Chain it after the OHS (obsidian-hybrid-search) `search` tool: pass its results as `hits` ([{"path", "score"}], or plain paths, in OHS order). Returns the hits re-ranked by graph support (found_by "ohs") and notes only the graph reached (found_by "graph": what text search missed), each with `via` = the shortest edge chain from a hit. Without hits, `query` is searched with the OHS index if this server can reach it; otherwise call OHS search first.
